content:
Penalties for not keeping your bank balance? ₹7,086 crore says it adds up.

That number stopped me.

Because ₹7,086 crore isn’t what banks earned from loans, investments or credit cards.

It was collected from customers who didn’t maintain the required minimum balance in their accounts.

Private sector banks accounted for ₹4,948.71 crore.

Public sector banks collected another ₹2,137.92 crore.

And that’s where this gets interesting.

For one customer, it might be ₹300.

Or ₹500.

An amount small enough to ignore.

But when millions of these “small” deductions come together, you get ₹7,086 crore.

That’s the thing about money.

The biggest financial leaks don’t always look big when they happen.

A bank charge here.
A subscription there.
A convenience fee you barely notice.

None of them feel expensive individually.

Until you add them up.

₹7,086 crore is what “small” can look like at scale.

Maybe checking your bank statement isn’t such a boring habit after all.
comment: The larger issue is transparency and choice. Many customers don't realize these rules until charges appear. Better alerts and simpler account options could prevent avoidable losses.
